doc.title: Vince Lateano interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002

title: Playing with Benny Carter
summary: He played with Carter at Yoshi's and Bimbo's; Carter's class and mastery.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: I played with him on two occasions. I played a weekend with him at Yoshi’s — or maybe more. Mel Martin, the saxophone player from the area, put together some stuff for Benny and there was — one was a big band gig right around the corner here at a place called Bimbo’s. And he put together a big band so we played Benny’s big band book and he was, is, just you talk about somebody that wouldn’t fit the mold of a tortured jazz musician, this is a real class act. Benny is a composer, a film writer, and he’s — I think one of his mottos is always go first class. Ask Phil Woods. He says that. And he does. And he doesn’t settle for less and he’s impeccable. And he plays that way. He plays so beautifully. And it was one of those situations where you know you’re in the presence of a master. Dizzy’s like that and people like that.
You treasure that moment for sure.
Exactly. But that’s Benny Carter. And his music of course is without saying, some of the most beautiful music in the world.
Yeah, it’s interesting, being with a guy like that, you think about his history being in Europe back in the 30s. What kind of experiences he’s had.

Yeah. And like he just came through it with flying colors. He just never lost his class. People are so respectful and deservedly so. And it’s a lesson. You don’t have to be anything other than a classy individual.
